title: The CAP theorem applied to data platforms

videos.script: Roda Livre keeps three copies of how many bicycles each station holds. {{three-copies}} One morning the link to one of those copies is cut, though nothing has crashed and all three machines are still running. {{cut}} A customer returns a bicycle at Rua XV, and her phone reaches the copy that is cut off. That copy has two choices. It can refuse, because it cannot check with the others. Or it can answer with only what it knows. {{two-choices}} That is the CAP theorem. When the network splits, each copy either stays correct or keeps answering, and nobody can promise you both. {{theorem}} In this lesson you cut that link yourself, and watch three copies behave in two different ways. Then the link comes back, and two histories have to become one. {{run}} After that you decide what each part of Roda Livre needs. Payments refuse, and the dock map answers. {{roda}} And then the course closes, with all ten lessons laid out as one map, each region beside the course that walks it next. {{map}}
